content:
Talia Benson: Dropping ADR draft for baseline artifact versioning (ADR-001). Would love quick eyes from Runtime + Release Eng before we publish. Main questions: what exactly we pin, where artifacts live, and what “reproducible” means for us.

Talia Benson: Link (Confluence draft): https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/display/ENGSR/ADR-001+Baseline+Artifact+Versioning

Marcus Reed: skimmed. +1 on having a single “baseline artifact bundle” concept. One request: call out the *minimum* required fields for a run to be considered comparable, vs “nice to have”.

Marcus Reed: e.g. required: workload suite version, traffic shape id, model id + quant profile, runtime commit/build id, CUDA/driver, GPU sku, region, seeds. optional: kernel autotune cache dump.

Mateo Alvarez: reading now. high level this is exactly what we need. Our biggest pain in Run 0 was “we think we changed nothing” but driver drift + fleet mix changed underneath.

Mateo Alvarez: Can we be explicit that baseline comparisons are only valid within a “hardware cohort”? Like H100-SXM vs H100-PCIe should be different baselines.

Vanessa Ortiz: yes please. also add memory size + clock caps where relevant (we’ve seen power cap differences across fleet pools). Doesn’t need to block runs, but should be recorded.

Connor O'Brien: release eng POV: I want the ADR to clearly define what the release qualification checklist needs to validate.

Connor O'Brien: Specifically:
- artifact bundle exists and is immutable
- runner recorded environment pins
- results link back to git SHA + build pipeline
- retention policy guarantees we can reproduce for at least N weeks after release

Sahana Iyer: +1. also we should name who “owns” refreshing baselines when we intentionally change the environment (driver upgrade, new base AMI, new instance type).

Sahana Iyer: otherwise CI/perf-canary will just start screaming and we’ll be in exception hell.

Allison Grant: On the observability side: please keep the metadata schema tight. We can store rich metadata as a JSON blob in object storage, but only promote a bounded set of labels into metrics.

Allison Grant: If we make `workload_prompt_set_hash` or `git_dirty_state` into a label we’ll blow up cardinality.

Logan Wright: ADR mentions “telemetry schema version” — I’d like to keep that. TTFT/TPOT derivation has changed already once. If the pipeline changes, we need to annotate baseline comparisons.

Marcus Reed: re: where artifacts live — ADR says “S3 + mirrored to GCS for some teams” which sounds messy.

Marcus Reed: suggest: one canonical bucket + path convention, and optional mirrors as a *consumer* thing, not producer.

Talia Benson: ack. Will simplify to canonical object storage location + a “how to fetch” snippet. Mirrors out of scope.

Mateo Alvarez: Another thing: immutability. If we rely on “latest” pointers anywhere, it’ll bite us.

Mateo Alvarez: can we make baseline bundles content-addressed? (hash in the path) + signed manifest.

Connor O'Brien: content-addressed path is great. For release qualification I mainly need stable identifiers to put into the release notes / checklist.

Connor O'Brien: Something like `baseline_suite=v0.3.1`, `baseline_id=q1_2026_lock_01`, `runtime_sha=...`.

Sahana Iyer: +1 manifest file. and please specify that reruns must create a new bundle id (even if config is “same”). otherwise we can’t debug variance.

Vanessa Ortiz: +1. variance investigation needs run-to-run traceability.

Allison Grant: strongly recommend: manifest as a single line-delimited JSON (or plain JSON) file in the bundle root. Easy to parse for dashboards.

Logan Wright: also include a `metrics_pipeline_sha` (or deploy version). if we can’t do SHA, at least a semver build id.

Marcus Reed: nit: the ADR currently says “pin kernel autotune results”. Are we actually able to do that reliably? kernels team said autotune cache sometimes varies across driver.

Mateo Alvarez: I’d phrase as: pin runtime’s kernel selection mode + seeds, and *record* autotune cache artifacts when available. Don’t make it required for baseline validity in v1.

Talia Benson: makes sense. I’ll move autotune cache to optional/diagnostic.

Connor O'Brien: can we add a section: “What changes require baseline refresh” vs “what changes just get recorded”? e.g.
- requires refresh: new GPU SKU / new driver major / major runtime scheduling behavior change (?)
- record-only: new dashboard panels, minor runner update

Sahana Iyer: careful on “major runtime scheduling behavior change” — we can’t refresh baseline on every perf PR. maybe: baselines refresh on *intentional* baseline update with sign-off.

Mateo Alvarez: agree. baseline should be stable reference; changes go through regression policy + explicit baseline bump.

Talia Benson: ok: I’ll define baseline refresh triggers as environment/fleet cohort changes and planned quarterly resets, plus an explicit “baseline update” process for real perf shifts.

Allison Grant: pls include sign-off list (Runtime + SRE + Release Eng) for baseline bump. even if lightweight.

Marcus Reed: +1. For this ADR, I think we’re aligned.

Talia Benson: awesome. I’ll incorporate comments today and mark for final review. If no blockers by EOD, publishing tomorrow.

Connor O'Brien: :thumbsup: ping me on the updated draft, I’ll do a final pass.

Sahana Iyer: :thumbsup:

Mateo Alvarez: :thumbsup:
